question: Gandhi founded which organisation in 1894 to protest against the discriminatory treatment of Indians in South Africa?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Natal Indian Congress.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 1894 Gandhi established the Natal Indian Congress in Durban to organise Indians against the oppressive measures of the white government (नटाल इंडियन कांग्रेस — दक्षिण अफ्रीका में गांधी द्वारा स्थापित संगठन)

 

• He had reached South Africa in 1893 to fight a lawsuit on behalf of the firm of Dada Abdullah & Company, and stayed on for about twenty-one years.

 

• The body used petitions and peaceful protest, an early rehearsal of the non-violent methods he later applied in India.

 

• The humiliation at Pietermaritzburg station, where he was thrown out of a first-class compartment, pushed him into the struggle against racial discrimination.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gandhi started the weekly Indian Opinion in 1903 to give a voice to the Indian community in South Africa.

 

• His first organised Satyagraha was launched in 1906 against the compulsory registration of Indians in the Transvaal.

 

• The Natal Indian Congress was modelled on the Indian National Congress, whose name he deliberately borrowed.

 

• Gandhi's stay in South Africa lasted from 1893 to 1914, after which he sailed to India via London.

 

NOTE

 

• Transvaal British Indian Association (Option 1): The Transvaal British Indian Association was the body through which the 1906 Transvaal struggle was fought, but the 1894 organisation in Natal province was a different, earlier body.

 

• Indian Opinion Society (Option 3): Indian Opinion was a newspaper begun in 1903, not a political association, and no society with that name was set up as the protest platform in 1894.

 

• Phoenix Settlement Committee (Option 4): The Phoenix Settlement near Durban was an ashram-community begun in 1904 for communal living and printing the paper; it was never a political congress.

question: Gandhi shaped Satyagraha into a method of protest at a farm near Johannesburg in 1910. What was this farm called?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tolstoy Farm.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tolstoy Farm, established in 1910 near Johannesburg, was a cooperative settlement for the families of Satyagrahis jailed in the Transvaal struggle (टॉलस्टॉय फार्म — जोहान्सबर्ग में गांधी का आश्रम, 1910)

 

• The farm was named after the Russian writer Leo Tolstoy, whose ideas on simple living and non-violence deeply influenced Gandhi.

 

• Residents did manual labour, shared chores and followed strict discipline, which trained volunteers for later passive resistance.

 

• It was financed by his German-Jewish friend Hermann Kallenbach, who gave the land for the experiment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The earlier community, Phoenix Settlement, was founded in 1904 near Durban in Natal.

 

• After returning to India Gandhi opened the Satyagraha Ashram at Ahmedabad in 1915, shifted to Sabarmati in 1917.

 

• His book Hind Swaraj (1909) was written aboard a ship returning from London.

 

• Hermann Kallenbach, an architect, bought the land and gave it to the Satyagrahis for use during the struggle.

 

NOTE

 

• Phoenix Farm (Option 1): Phoenix Settlement was the 1904 community near Durban, in Natal; it is the earlier ashram and not the Johannesburg farm where Satyagraha was given shape in 1910.

 

• Sabarmati Farm (Option 2): Sabarmati was the Ahmedabad ashram of 1917 in India, and Gandhi had already left South Africa for good in 1914, so it could not be the 1910 farm.

 

• Kocharab Farm (Option 4): Kocharab was the first Ahmedabad ashram premises of 1915, a bungalow in the Paldi area; it lay in India and has no connection to the South African experiments.

question:
Match the publication of Gandhi with its year.

Column A: (a) Indian Opinion (b) Hind Swaraj (c) Young India (d) Harijan

Column B: (i) 1909 (ii) 1919 (iii) 1903 (iv) 1933
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Indian Opinion was brought out in 1903 in South Africa; Hind Swaraj was written in 1909; Young India started in 1919; Harijan appeared in 1933 (गांधी की पत्र-पत्रिकाएँ और पुस्तकें — वर्ष सहित)

 

• Indian Opinion served the Indian community in Natal and the Transvaal, and was printed at the Phoenix Settlement.

 

• Hind Swaraj, a short book in the form of a dialogue between the Reader and the Editor, criticised modern civilisation and set out his idea of swaraj.

 

• Young India was the English weekly through which he later wrote on Bardoli, while Harijan was the weekly connected with the campaign for the so-called untouchables.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gandhi's autobiography My Experiments with Truth was first written in Gujarati and serialised in his journal.

 

• Navajivan, a Gujarati weekly, was also edited by him from 1919.

 

• He gave the name Harijan (children of God) to the depressed classes and founded the Harijan Sevak Sangh.

 

• Gandhi's other major book, The Story of My Experiments with Truth, was written in the 1920s in prison and at Yerwada.

 

NOTE

 

• a-i, b-iii, c-ii, d-iv (Option 1): This key places Indian Opinion in 1909 and Hind Swaraj in 1903, which reverses the two earliest items; the newspaper began in 1903 and the book was written six years later.

 

• a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii (Option 2): Here Young India is paired with 1933 and Harijan with 1919, but the English weekly began in 1919 while the journal named for the depressed classes began in 1933.

 

• a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv (Option 3): This combination shifts every item by a wrong year, giving Indian Opinion 1919 and Young India 1909; Young India could not exist before Gandhi returned to India.

question: Pravasi Bharatiya Divas is observed on 9 January because on that date in 1915 which event took place?
option_2: Gandhi returned to India from South Africa
option_4: Gandhi was awarded the Kaiser-i-Hind medal
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gandhi returned to India from South Africa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gandhi arrived at Bombay from South Africa on 9 January 1915, and the date is celebrated as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas, the Non-Resident Indian Day (प्रवासी भारतीय दिवस — गांधी की स्वदेश वापसी, 9 जनवरी 1915)

 

• He had spent about twenty-one years in South Africa, leading the struggle against racial discrimination before returning.

 

• On his advice from Gokhale he toured India for a year to understand the country before joining politics.

 

• Soon afterwards he opened the Satyagraha Ashram at Ahmedabad in 1915, which moved to Sabarmati in 1917.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale became his political mentor and guide.

 

• The first Satyagraha on Indian soil was the Champaran movement of 1917.

 

• Pravasi Bharatiya Divas conventions began in 2003 and are held to honour the Indian diaspora.

 

• The first Pravasi Bharatiya Divas convention was held in New Delhi in January 2003.

 

NOTE

 

• Gandhi started the Champaran Satyagraha (Option 1): The Champaran Satyagraha began in 1917, two years after his arrival, when Rajkumar Shukla persuaded him to visit Bihar to see the plight of indigo cultivators.

 

• Gandhi established Sabarmati Ashram (Option 3): Sabarmati Ashram was set up in 1917 on the bank of the river near Ahmedabad; the ashram was first opened at Kochrab in 1915, so the date does not mark it.

 

• Gandhi was awarded the Kaiser-i-Hind medal (Option 4): The Kaiser-i-Hind medal was conferred on him in 1915 for his ambulance corps work in the war, but it was not given on 9 January and has no link with the diaspora day.

question:
Consider the following statements about Gandhi after his return to India:

1. He was awarded the Kaiser-i-Hind medal in 1915 for his ambulance corps work during the First World War.

2. Gopal Krishna Gokhale became his political guru.

3. Satyagraha Ashram was moved to Sabarmati in 1917.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 2 and 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Gandhi raised an ambulance corps during the First World War and received the Kaiser-i-Hind medal from Viceroy Hardinge in 1915 (गांधी को 1915 में कैसर-ए-हिंद पदक मिला)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: after meeting Gopal Krishna Gokhale, Gandhi accepted him as his political mentor and followed his advice to study India before taking any political position.

 

• Statement 3 is correct: the Satyagraha Ashram opened at Ahmedabad in 1915 and was relocated to the bank of the Sabarmati in 1917.

 

• All three statements hold, so the combination covering every statement is right.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kaiser-i-Hind medal had been instituted in 1900 for public service in India.

 

• Gandhi later returned the medal at the start of the Non-Cooperation Movement.

 

• Because of his wartime help, Gandhi was jokingly called the recruiting 'Sergeant' of the army.

 

• Hardinge, the Viceroy who gave the medal, was also the one who survived a bomb attack in Delhi in 1912.

 

NOTE

 

• 1 and 2 only (Option 2): Dropping statement 3 is wrong because the Ahmedabad ashram was indeed shifted to the Sabarmati riverbank in 1917, so excluding it leaves one true statement unaccounted for.

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 3): Leaving out the first statement is incorrect since the 1915 medal for his ambulance corps is well established, and he later surrendered it in 1920.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 4): Dropping statement 2 is wrong because Gokhale, founder of the Servants of India Society, is universally accepted as his political guru in India.

question: The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 was launched against which exploitative system imposed on peasants by European planters?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tinkathia system.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the Tinkathia system European indigo planters forced peasants of Champaran, Bihar, to grow indigo on three-twentieths (3 kathas per bigha) of their land (तिनकठिया प्रथा — चंपारण सत्याग्रह 1917)

 

• On the invitation of Rajkumar Shukla, Gandhi reached Champaran and the government appointed an inquiry in which he was a member.

 

• The system was abolished and the peasants got back 25 per cent of the illegally collected money as compensation.

 

• It was the first Satyagraha in India; during this campaign the people began calling him Bapu and Mahatma.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rajendra Prasad, Brajkishore Prasad and J.B. Kripalani assisted Gandhi in Champaran.

 

• Rabindranath Tagore is credited with the title Mahatma, according to many accounts.

 

• The Champaran Agrarian Act of 1918 gave legal form to the reforms.

 

• Champaran also gave Gandhi the support of young lawyers like Rajendra Prasad, who joined the national movement because of it.

 

NOTE

 

• Ryotwari system (Option 1): The Ryotwari system was a land revenue arrangement of Madras and Bombay in which the government settled revenue directly with cultivators, and it did not involve forced indigo cultivation.

 

• Zamindari system (Option 2): The Zamindari system concerned intermediaries who collected rent in Bengal and Bihar; the indigo grievance in Champaran arose from planter contracts rather than from zamindari rent.

 

• Permanent Settlement (Option 4): The Permanent Settlement of 1793 fixed revenue permanently with zamindars under Cornwallis, long before 1917, and it is not the system targeted by the Champaran struggle.

question: In the Ahmedabad Mill Strike of 1918, Gandhi used which method of protest for the first time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fast unto death (hunger strike).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gandhi resorted to a fast unto death for the first time during the Ahmedabad Mill Strike, a labour dispute between mill owners and workers (अहमदाबाद मिल हड़ताल 1918 — गांधी का पहला अनशन)

 

• The owners wanted to withdraw the plague bonus, while workers demanded a 50 per cent rise in wages.

 

• The mill owner Ambalal Sarabhai opposed the workers, though his sister Anusuya Ben supported Gandhi.

 

• After the fast the owners agreed to a 35 per cent increase in salary.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Anusuya Sarabhai later founded the Majur Mahajan Sangh, the Textile Labour Association of Ahmedabad.

 

• The Ahmedabad strike was a purely labour movement, unlike Champaran which was an agrarian one.

 

• Gandhi's other major fast in this period was in 1932 against separate electorates for the depressed classes.

 

• The Ahmedabad dispute was settled by arbitration, a method the Textile Labour Association later adopted for its disputes.

 

NOTE

 

• Dandi-style long march (Option 2): The march method was used in 1930 at Dandi to break the Salt Act, twelve years after the mill strike, so it cannot be the first use in 1918.

 

• Boycott of foreign cloth (Option 3): Boycott of foreign cloth emerged mainly with the Swadeshi movement of 1905 and later Non-Cooperation, not as the feature of the Ahmedabad labour dispute.

 

• Mass civil disobedience (Option 4): Mass civil disobedience was launched on a national scale in 1930; the mill dispute was a local settlement achieved through a fast and negotiation.

question: Which leader led the Kheda Satyagraha of 1918 in Gujarat on Gandhi's behalf, protesting against land revenue collection after crop failure?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vallabhbhai Patel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 1918 the Kheda district faced crop failure due to drought, yet the government refused to grant revenue remission, though rules permitted it when produce was below one-fourth of normal (खेड़ा सत्याग्रह 1918 — वल्लभभाई पटेल)

 

• Gandhi came on the invitation of Vallabhbhai Patel, and under his guidance Patel led the no-tax campaign among Patidar peasants.

 

• Along with Champaran and Ahmedabad, Kheda showed Gandhi's ability to mobilise farmers, artisans and workers.

 

• The government eventually agreed to suspend collection from poorer peasants.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Patel was later given the title Sardar during the Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928.

 

• Indulal Yagnik and Narhari Parikh were other local workers in Kheda.

 

• Patel later became the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of independent India.

 

• Kheda is regarded by many writers as an early experiment in non-cooperation, because peasants refused to pay revenue.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajendra Prasad (Option 1): Rajendra Prasad worked with Gandhi in Champaran, Bihar in 1917, and later became the first President of India, but he was not the leader in Kheda.

 

• Mahadev Desai (Option 2): Mahadev Desai was Gandhi's secretary and biographer, serving as his close aide, though he was not the figure who led the Kheda tax resistance.

 

• Jawaharlal Nehru (Option 3): Jawaharlal Nehru first met Gandhi in 1916 and became active only during the Rowlatt and Non-Cooperation period, so he took no part in Kheda.

question: Arrange the following events in chronological order.
option_1: Champaran Satyagraha – Rowlatt Satyagraha hartal – Chauri Chaura incident – Dandi March
option_2: Rowlatt Satyagraha hartal – Champaran Satyagraha – Dandi March – Chauri Chaura incident
option_3: Champaran Satyagraha – Chauri Chaura incident – Rowlatt Satyagraha hartal – Dandi March
option_4: Rowlatt Satyagraha hartal – Champaran Satyagraha – Chauri Chaura incident – Dandi March
solution_text:
The correct answer is Champaran Satyagraha – Rowlatt Satyagraha hartal – Chauri Chaura incident – Dandi March.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Champaran Satyagraha came first, in 1917 (पहला क्रम: चंपारण 1917, फिर रौलट हड़ताल 1919, चौरी चौरा 1922, दांडी 1930)

 

• The nationwide hartal against the Rowlatt Act was held on 6 April 1919, in the aftermath of the First World War.

 

• The Chauri Chaura incident of 4 February 1922 led Gandhi to suspend the Non-Cooperation Movement.

 

• The Dandi March started on 12 March 1930 and opened the Civil Disobedience Movement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gandhi was arrested on 10 March 1922 and sentenced to six years, but was released in February 1924 on health grounds.

 

• The Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 13 April 1919 took place a week after the hartal.

 

• Salt law was broken at Dandi on 6 April 1930.

 

• The Rowlatt Satyagraha and the Jallianwala massacre drove Gandhi to take the lead of the Congress from 1920.

 

NOTE

 

• Rowlatt Satyagraha hartal – Champaran Satyagraha – Dandi March – Chauri Chaura incident (Option 2): This ordering places the 1919 hartal ahead of Champaran, though the Bihar peasant movement of 1917 was Gandhi's first Indian Satyagraha and so must come before 1919.

 

• Champaran Satyagraha – Chauri Chaura incident – Rowlatt Satyagraha hartal – Dandi March (Option 3): Here Chauri Chaura is placed before the Rowlatt hartal, which is impossible because the incident of February 1922 occurred nearly three years after the April 1919 hartal.

 

• Rowlatt Satyagraha hartal – Champaran Satyagraha – Chauri Chaura incident – Dandi March (Option 4): The sequence begins with the Rowlatt hartal of 1919, whereas Champaran in 1917 was earlier; only the last two items of this ordering happen to be placed correctly.

question: Which of the following did NOT resign from the Imperial Legislative Council in protest against the passing of the Rowlatt Act?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rowlatt Act was passed in 1919 despite the unanimous opposition of the Indian members, and Malaviya, Jinnah and Mazhar-ul-Haq resigned in protest (रौलट एक्ट के विरोध में इस्तीफा देने वाले सदस्य)

 

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak was not a member of the Imperial Legislative Council at that time and did not take part in these resignations.

 

• The Act allowed detention of suspects for two years without trial and searches without warrants, and was called the Black Act.

 

• Gandhi responded by calling an all-India hartal on 6 April 1919, the Rowlatt Satyagraha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Act is formally the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919, based on the Sedition Committee Report headed by Justice Rowlatt.

 

• The Act was passed in March 1919 by the Imperial Legislative Council, in which the official majority outvoted all Indian members.

 

• Gandhi formed the Satyagraha Sabha to oppose it.

 

• The Rowlatt Act did not give the right of appeal, nor the right to a lawyer or an open trial, to the accused.

 

NOTE

 

• Madan Mohan Malaviya (Option 1): Madan Mohan Malaviya is a recorded member who quit the Imperial Legislative Council over the Rowlatt Act, so he is wrongly picked as the person who did not resign.

 

• Muhammad Ali Jinnah (Option 2): Muhammad Ali Jinnah resigned from the Council in March 1919, writing that a government that passes such a law in peace time forfeits claim to be civilised.

 

• Mazhar-ul-Haq (Option 4): Mazhar-ul-Haq, a Bihar barrister and nationalist Muslim, resigned along with Malaviya and Jinnah, so he cannot be the exception asked for.

question: The arrest of which two Congress leaders in April 1919 triggered protests that led to the Jallianwala Bagh gathering?
option_1: Lala Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh
option_2: Dr. Satyapal and Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dr. Satyapal and Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• On 10 April 1919 the Punjab government arrested Dr. Satya Pal and Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew, two popular leaders of Amritsar (सत्यपाल और सैफुद्दीन किचलू की गिरफ्तारी — अमृतसर, अप्रैल 1919)

 

• Protests broke out in the city and on 13 April 1919, the day of Baisakhi, a public meeting was called at Jallianwala Bagh.

 

• General Dyer blocked the narrow entrance and ordered his troops to fire on the unarmed crowd without warning.

 

• The Hunter Committee put the official figure at 379 dead and 1,137 injured.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sir Michael O'Dwyer, Lieutenant Governor of Punjab, backed Dyer's action; Udham Singh killed him in London in 1940.

 

• Gandhi had called off the Rowlatt Satyagraha following violence in several provinces.

 

• Martial law was proclaimed in Punjab after the unrest.

 

• Dr. Kitchlew was later a Khilafat leader, and he served as president of the All India Peace Council in the 1950s.

 

NOTE

 

• Lala Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh (Option 1): Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh were Punjab agitators deported in 1907 over the Colonization Bill, a decade before this episode, and were not the leaders arrested in 1919.

 

• Motilal Nehru and C.R. Das (Option 3): Motilal Nehru and C.R. Das were Congress leaders in Allahabad and Calcutta, and later founded the Swaraj Party; they were not arrested at Amritsar then.

 

• Shaukat Ali and Muhammad Ali (Option 4): Shaukat Ali and Muhammad Ali were the Khilafat leaders who were interned during the First World War; their detention had no link with the Amritsar protests of April 1919.

question: Michael O'Dwyer, who had supported General Dyer's action at Jallianwala Bagh, was assassinated in London in 1940 by
solution_text:
The correct answer is Udham Singh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Udham Singh shot dead Sir Michael O'Dwyer, former Lieutenant Governor of Punjab, at Caxton Hall, London, in 1940 (उधम सिंह द्वारा माइकल ओ'डायर की हत्या, 1940)

 

• O'Dwyer was the Punjab official who approved of Dyer's firing on the crowd at Jallianwala Bagh on 13 April 1919.

 

• Udham Singh, a survivor and eyewitness of the massacre, took revenge after two decades and was hanged in 1940.

 

• General Dyer himself was relieved from service after the Hunter Committee and died in England in 1927.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Madan Lal Dhingra shot Curzon Wyllie in London in 1909.

 

• Khudiram Bose threw a bomb at Kingsford's carriage in Muzaffarpur in 1908.

 

• Dyer was praised by the Morning Post, which raised about 26,000 pounds for him.

 

• Udham Singh used the name Ram Mohammad Singh Azad to show the unity of religions, and was hanged at Pentonville in July 1940.

 

NOTE

 

• Madan Lal Dhingra (Option 1): Madan Lal Dhingra killed Sir William Curzon Wyllie, an India Office aide, in London in 1909, which is a different incident with no link to Punjab.

 

• Khudiram Bose (Option 2): Khudiram Bose attempted to kill the magistrate Kingsford at Muzaffarpur in 1908 and was hanged at the age of eighteen; he had nothing to do with 1940.

 

• Batukeshwar Dutt (Option 3): Batukeshwar Dutt threw bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly with Bhagat Singh in 1929 and lived until 1965, so he was not the assassin of O'Dwyer.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding the aftermath of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre:

1. The Hunter Committee condemned Dyer's action but no disciplinary action was taken.

2. Rabindranath Tagore renounced his knighthood in protest.

3. The Hunter Committee was set up to inquire into the Rowlatt Act.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 holds: the Hunter Committee of eight members, formed to investigate the massacre, censured Dyer but proposed no punishment, and the Punjab government cleared him (हंटर कमेटी — डायर की निंदा, पर कार्रवाई नहीं)

 

• Statement 2 holds: Tagore gave up his knighthood in protest, and Gandhi also returned his titles.

 

• Statement 3 is wrong: the committee was appointed to inquire into the massacre and the disturbances in Punjab, not into the Rowlatt Act, which had already been passed.

 

• Thus only statements 1 and 2 are correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Congress appointed its own non-official inquiry committee which included Gandhi, Motilal Nehru and C.R. Das.

 

• The official Hunter figure of 379 dead is lower than Indian estimates of well over a thousand.

 

• The Sedition Committee under Justice Rowlatt had earlier produced the report that led to the Rowlatt Act.

 

• The Hunter Committee was chaired by Lord William Hunter, and it had both British and Indian members.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 1): The combination of statements 2 and 3 is incorrect because the third claim is false, as the Hunter Committee investigated Punjab disorders and Jallianwala Bagh rather than the Rowlatt Act.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 2): Pairing statements 1 and 3 drops the true claim about Tagore's knighthood and keeps the false claim about the committee's purpose, which makes the combination unacceptable.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): Selecting all three fails because the third is untrue; the committee was never charged with reviewing the Rowlatt law, which was reviewed in the Sedition Committee Report instead.

question: The Khilafat Movement in India was initiated by which pair of brothers?
option_3: Hakim Ajmal Khan and Rafi Ahmad Kidwai
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shaukat Ali and Muhammad Ali.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ali brothers, Shaukat Ali and Muhammad Ali Jauhar, started the Khilafat agitation to protect the position of the Sultan of Turkey, regarded as the Khalifa (अली बंधु — खिलाफत आंदोलन के प्रणेता)

 

• Indian Muslims were angered when the Ottoman Empire was dismembered after the First World War and the Khalifa lost power, breaking the wartime assurance about Turkey's sacred places.

 

• A Khilafat Committee was formed, and 17 October 1919 was observed as Khilafat Day across the country.

 

• Other prominent supporters included Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, M.A. Ansari and Saifuddin Kitchlew.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gandhi presided over a joint Hindu-Muslim conference on 23 November 1919 at Delhi and backed the Khilafat cause.

 

• On 31 August 1920 Khilafat Day was observed, and Gandhi announced his non-cooperation plan.

 

• The Khilafat issue merged with the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920.

 

• Muhammad Ali Jauhar edited the papers Comrade and Hamdard, and Shaukat Ali later presided over the Khilafat Committee.

 

NOTE

 

• Hasrat Mohani and Zafar Ali (Option 2): Hasrat Mohani, who coined Inquilab Zindabad, and Zafar Ali were Urdu poets and journalists, not brothers, and neither pair headed the movement that Gandhi supported.

 

• Hakim Ajmal Khan and Rafi Ahmad Kidwai (Option 3): Hakim Ajmal Khan and Rafi Ahmad Kidwai were nationalist Muslim leaders associated with the Congress, but they were not the brothers who started the Khilafat agitation.

 

• Saifuddin Kitchlew and Mazhar-ul-Haq (Option 4): Kitchlew and Mazhar-ul-Haq were separate nationalist figures; Kitchlew was arrested in April 1919 at Amritsar, and the two were unrelated by family and not the founding duo.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Khilafat Movement:

1. Indian Muslims regarded the Sultan of Turkey as their spiritual leader, the Khalifa.

2. Turkey had fought on the side of Britain in the First World War.

3. The movement merged with the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 3 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Muslims across the world including India looked upon the Sultan of Turkey as the Khalifa, their spiritual head (खलीफा — तुर्की का सुल्तान)

 

• Statement 2 is incorrect: in the First World War, Turkey allied with Germany and Austria against Britain, and this made Indian Muslims anxious about Turkey's fate.

 

• Statement 3 is correct: Gandhi, keen on Hindu-Muslim unity, linked the Khilafat cause with the Non-Cooperation Movement of 1920.

 

• Hence only statements 1 and 3 are right.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Treaty of Sevres of 1920 reduced Turkey's territory and enraged the Muslims of India.

 

• The movement collapsed when Mustafa Kemal Pasha abolished the Caliphate in 1924.

 

• After the Chauri Chaura withdrawal of 1922 the Khilafat movement gradually disintegrated.

 

• The Khilafat delegation to Britain in 1920 led by Muhammad Ali failed to change British policy on Turkey.

 

NOTE

 

• 1 and 2 only (Option 1): Statements 1 and 2 together fail because Turkey was on the German side, not Britain's, in the war; that wrong claim is what makes this pair unacceptable.

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 3): Statements 2 and 3 cannot both be accepted since the claim about Turkey fighting alongside Britain is false, even though the merger with Non-Cooperation is accurate.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): Choosing all three fails because Turkey joined Germany and Austria, so Indian Muslims' support to Britain was based on a promise that was later betrayed.

question: Which of the following was NOT a part of the Non-Cooperation Movement programme?
option_1: Boycott of government schools and colleges
option_2: Surrender of titles and honorary positions
option_4: Boycott of foreign goods and promotion of khadi
solution_text:
The correct answer is Breaking the Salt Law.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Violation of the Salt Law belonged to the Civil Disobedience Movement of 1930, launched with the Dandi March, and was not part of the 1920-22 programme (नमक कानून भंग — सविनय अवज्ञा आंदोलन, असहयोग नहीं)

 

• The Non-Cooperation Movement included surrender of titles, resignation from local bodies and boycott of elections under the 1919 Act.

 

• It also called for boycott of courts, schools and colleges, and foreign cloth, along with national schools, panchayat courts and khadi.

 

• Lawyers like C.R. Das, Motilal Nehru, Rajendra Prasad and Vallabhbhai Patel gave up practice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Imports of foreign cloth fell drastically between 1920 and 1922.

 

• Almost 60,000 people were arrested during the movement.

 

• Tagore gave up his knighthood and Gandhi returned the Kaiser-i-Hind medal.

 

• Foreign cloth was burnt in bonfires; the first big bonfire was held in Bombay in July 1921 at Gandhi's instance.

 

NOTE

 

• Boycott of government schools and colleges (Option 1): Boycott of government schools and colleges was a central constructive-negative item of the 1920 programme, leading to the setting up of Jamia Millia, Kashi Vidyapith and others.

 

• Surrender of titles and honorary positions (Option 2): Giving up titles and honorary offices was among the first steps; Gandhi returned his Kaiser-i-Hind and Tagore his knighthood, so this cannot be the exception.

 

• Boycott of foreign goods and promotion of khadi (Option 4): Foreign cloth boycott together with spinning and khadi was the soul of the movement, and the charkha became a common household item through it.

question: The Chauri Chaura incident, after which Gandhi suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement, took place in which district of Uttar Pradesh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gorakhpur.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• On 4 February 1922 at Chauri Chaura in the Gorakhpur district, police fired on a procession of volunteers, and the angry crowd set the police station on fire, killing 22 policemen (गोरखपुर का चौरी चौरा कांड, 4 फरवरी 1922)

 

• Deeply disturbed by the violence, Gandhi decided on 12 February 1922 to suspend the movement, at the Bardoli meeting of the Congress Working Committee.

 

• A session court sentenced 172 of 225 accused to death, a harsh verdict that shocked national opinion.

 

• Gandhi himself was arrested on 10 March 1922 and sentenced to six years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Subhas Bose and Lala Lajpat Rai criticised the withdrawal of the movement.

 

• Motilal Nehru and C.R. Das also opposed it, leading to a split in the Gaya Congress of December 1922.

 

• In 2022 the centenary of the Chauri Chaura incident was commemorated nationwide.

 

• The local volunteers had been protesting against the high price of food and liquor shops when police opened fire.

 

NOTE

 

• Meerut (Option 1): Meerut was the place where the Revolt of 1857 began and the 1929 conspiracy case was tried, so it is a famous city but not where the 1922 police station was burnt.

 

• Kanpur (Option 3): Kanpur saw the founding of the Hindustan Republican Association in 1924, which is a revolutionary event unrelated to the burning of the police post in 1922.

 

• Lucknow (Option 4): Lucknow is the capital, near which the Kakori action happened in 1925; the Chauri Chaura episode did not occur in this district, which lies far to the east.

question:
Assertion (A): Gandhi suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement in February 1922.

Reason (R): Violence took place at Chauri Chaura, in which a mob burnt a police station and killed policemen.
option_1: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_2: A is true but R is false
option_3: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
option_4: A is false but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion A is true: on 12 February 1922 Gandhi formally halted the Non-Cooperation Movement (असहयोग आंदोलन की वापसी, फरवरी 1922)

 

• Reason R is also true: on 4 February 1922 a crowd at Chauri Chaura set fire to the police station and 22 policemen were killed.

 

• R explains A because Gandhi insisted on strict non-violence and felt the people were not ready for civil disobedience when violence broke out.

 

• Leaders such as Motilal Nehru, Lajpat Rai and Subhas Bose criticised the decision, but it was the violence that triggered it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The withdrawal caused a rift between the Congress and the Muslim League and weakened the Khilafat movement.

 

• Many frustrated youths turned toward revolutionary activity after 1922.

 

• Gandhi was arrested on 10 March 1922 for sedition.

 

• Gandhi's phrase 'Himalayan blunder' was used in 1919 after the Rowlatt agitation turned violent, so the idea of premature mass action recurs in his thinking.

 

NOTE

 

• Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A (Option 1): The statement that R fails to explain A is wrong because the massacre of policemen was the immediate and acknowledged reason Gandhi gave for withdrawal.

 

• A is true but R is false (Option 2): Calling A true and R false cannot be right since the burning of the police station with 22 policemen inside is a documented fact of 4 February 1922.

 

• A is false but R is true (Option 4): Treating A as false is incorrect as the suspension was announced by Gandhi at Bardoli on 12 February 1922 and is one of the best-known turning points.

question: The Swaraj Party was formed on 1 January 1923 by
option_1: Lala Lajpat Rai and Madan Mohan Malaviya
option_2: Subhas Chandra Bose and Jawaharlal Nehru
solution_text:
The correct answer is C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Following the suspension of Non-Cooperation, Congress split at the Gaya session of December 1922, and C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru formed the Swaraj Party on 1 January 1923 (स्वराज पार्टी — चित्तरंजन दास और मोतीलाल नेहरू)

 

• C.R. Das was the President and Motilal Nehru the Secretary; the group wished to enter the legislative councils and wreck them from within.

 

• The No-Changers, led by Rajendra Prasad, Patel and Rajagopalachari, opposed council entry and favoured constructive work.

 

• In November 1924 the Gandhi-Das Pact brought the Swaraj Party and the Congress together.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gandhi, after release in 1924, supported council entry.

 

• The Swaraj Party won a large number of seats in the 1923 elections to the Central Legislative Assembly.

 

• Vithalbhai Patel, a Swarajist, became President of the Central Legislative Assembly in 1925.

 

• The Swarajists also formed a coalition with Muslim Swarajists in the Bengal Pact of 1923, which Das wanted to implement.

 

NOTE

 

• Lala Lajpat Rai and Madan Mohan Malaviya (Option 1): Lajpat Rai and Malaviya were associated with the Hindu Mahasabha and later the Independent Congress Party, and did not found the party with the council-entry plan.

 

• Subhas Chandra Bose and Jawaharlal Nehru (Option 2): Bose and Jawaharlal Nehru were younger leaders who in 1923 did not form the group; Bose worked under C.R. Das in Calcutta but was not a co-founder.

 

• Rajendra Prasad and Vallabhbhai Patel (Option 3): Prasad and Patel belonged to the No-Changers, who opposed entering legislatures, which makes them the rivals of the Swarajists rather than their founders.

question: Gandhi presided over the Indian National Congress session only once. At which place was that session held in 1924?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Belgaum.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gandhi's only presidency of the Congress was at the Belgaum session of 1924, in Karnataka (बेलगाम अधिवेशन 1924 — गांधी अध्यक्ष)

 

• The session followed the Gandhi-Das Pact of November 1924, under which Congress and the Swaraj Party agreed to work together and contest elections to the councils.

 

• Gandhi had been released in February 1924 on grounds of ill-health and, after the pact, accepted the council-entry strategy.

 

• His first Congress session visit was in 1901 at Calcutta, where he only observed.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Nagpur session of December 1920 is linked with the approval of Non-Cooperation.

 

• The Gaya session of 1922 saw the Swarajists' demand for council entry.

 

• The Lahore session of 1929 under Jawaharlal Nehru declared Purna Swaraj.

 

• Sarojini Naidu became the first Indian woman President of the Congress at Kanpur in 1925, the session after Gandhi's.

 

NOTE

 

• Nagpur (Option 1): Nagpur hosted the 1920 session, presided over by C. Vijayaraghavachariar, where the Non-Cooperation resolution was confirmed; Gandhi was not the president there.

 

• Gaya (Option 2): The Gaya session in December 1922 was presided over by C.R. Das, and it witnessed the clash between pro-council and anti-council groups.

 

• Lahore (Option 4): Lahore held the 1929 session under Jawaharlal Nehru, where the Purna Swaraj goal was proclaimed, which was nearly five years after Gandhi's term.

question: The Hindustan Republican Association was founded in 1924 at Kanpur by
option_2: Sachindra Nath Sanyal and Yogesh Chandra Chatterjee
option_4: Lala Hardayal and Rash Behari Bose
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sachindra Nath Sanyal and Yogesh Chandra Chatterjee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The HRA was formed in 1924 at Kanpur by Sachindra Nath Sanyal and Yogesh Chandra Chatterjee, with Ram Prasad Bismil in the early group (हिंदुस्तान रिपब्लिकन एसोसिएशन, 1924, कानपुर)

 

• The group chose violent means to overthrow British rule and decided to raise funds through robbery of banks and treasuries.

 

• Early members at the first meeting included Ram Prasad Bismil, Bhagat Singh and Chandra Shekhar Azad.

 

• Its most famous action was the Kakori train robbery of 1925; after that arrests crippled the organisation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sanyal wrote the manifesto The Revolutionary and the book Bandi Jivan.

 

• In 1928 the HRA was reorganised by Azad as the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association.

 

• The Naujawan Bharat Sabha was set up by Bhagat Singh and associates in Punjab in 1926.

 

• The HRA manifesto 'The Revolutionary' was distributed across northern India on the same night in January 1925.

 

NOTE

 

• Bhagat Singh and Sukhdev (Option 1): Bhagat Singh and Sukhdev were younger recruits who joined later and helped to rename it in 1928; they were not its founders in 1924.

 

• Chandra Shekhar Azad and Rajguru (Option 3): Azad and Rajguru were members and fighters of the later phase, but neither led the 1924 founding; Rajguru joined after the Kakori incident.

 

• Lala Hardayal and Rash Behari Bose (Option 4): Hardayal and Rash Behari Bose were leaders of the Ghadar movement and Delhi-Lahore conspiracy years earlier and were not behind the Kanpur body.

question: Which of the following revolutionaries was NOT hanged in connection with the Kakori train action of 1925?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chandra Shekhar Azad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kakori action of 9 August 1925 led to the hanging of Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Lal and Rajendra Lahiri, while Chandra Shekhar Azad evaded capture (काकोरी कांड — चार को फाँसी, आज़ाद फरार)

 

• Azad had helped plan the raid but remained a fugitive for years and died on 27 February 1931 in Alfred Park, Allahabad, shooting himself.

 

• The raid targeted the 8 Down train from Saharanpur to Lucknow and looted about 8,000 rupees from the guard's cabin.

 

• Bismil, the key conspirator, was arrested on 26 September 1925.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bismil is remembered for the patriotic verse Sarfaroshi ki Tamanna.

 

• The Uttar Pradesh government has renamed the incident as the Kakori Train Action.

 

• The HRA wished to fund its work and create a positive image among the people.

 

• Bismil's autobiography was written in Gorakhpur jail days before his execution and is regarded as a classic.

 

NOTE

 

• Ram Prasad Bismil (Option 1): Ram Prasad Bismil was the principal organiser and was hanged at Gorakhpur jail in December 1927, so he cannot be the one who escaped the gallows.

 

• Ashfaqullah Khan (Option 2): Ashfaqullah Khan, a close friend of Bismil, was arrested later and hanged at Faizabad in December 1927 for his part in the plan.

 

• Rajendra Lahiri (Option 4): Rajendra Lahiri was executed at Gonda jail in December 1927, two days ahead of the schedule, and thus is among those hanged for Kakori.

question: Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Azad killed J.P. Saunders at Lahore in 1928 to avenge the death of
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lala Lajpat Rai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lala Lajpat Rai was seriously injured in a police lathi-charge while leading a demonstration against the Simon Commission at Lahore on 30 October 1928 and died on 17 November 1928 (लाला लाजपत राय की मृत्यु का बदला — सॉन्डर्स वध)

 

• The HSRA, re-established by Chandra Shekhar Azad on 10 September 1928 at Firoz Shah Kotla in Delhi, planned to kill the officer held responsible, J.P. Saunders.

 

• Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Azad shot Saunders in Lahore, an assistant superintendent of police, in December 1928.

 

• This led to the Lahore Conspiracy Case.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Simon Commission was greeted with black flags and slogans of 'Simon Go Back'.

 

• Lajpat Rai is called Punjab Kesari and founded the Servants of the People Society.

 

• The lathi-charge was ordered by Superintendent James Scott.

 

• Bhagat Singh escaped from Lahore after the murder disguised as a European, with Durga Bhabhi as his companion.

 

NOTE

 

• Jatin Das (Option 1): Jatin Das died in September 1929 after a 63-day hunger strike in Lahore jail, which happened after the Saunders shooting, so he could not be the reason for it.

 

• Ram Prasad Bismil (Option 2): Ram Prasad Bismil was hanged in 1925 for Kakori; his death preceded the Saunders killing but it was not the cause of that plot, and he belonged to the HRA.

 

• Rajguru (Option 3): Rajguru participated in the Saunders shooting as a member of the group; he was a co-conspirator who was himself hanged in 1931, not the leader avenged.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Central Legislative Assembly bombing of 8 April 1929:

1. Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw the bombs.

2. The bombs were meant to kill the members of the Assembly.

3. It took place during discussions on the Public Safety Bill and the Trade Disputes Bill.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 3 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw the bombs in the Assembly hall in Delhi on 8 April 1929 (केंद्रीय असेंबली बम कांड — भगत सिंह और बटुकेश्वर दत्त)

 

• Statement 2 is incorrect: the bombs were made to be harmless; the revolutionaries did not aim to kill anybody but to make their voice heard, as they put it, to make the deaf hear.

 

• Statement 3 is correct: the incident occurred when the Assembly was debating the Public Safety Bill and the Trade Disputes Bill.

 

• Both men courted arrest by throwing leaflets and shouting 'Inquilab Zindabad'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Inquilab Zindabad was coined by Hasrat Mohani and popularised by Bhagat Singh.

 

• Jatin Das, arrested in the same period, died after a 63-day hunger strike demanding political prisoner status.

 

• Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were hanged on 23 March 1931, observed as Shaheed Diwas.

 

• Batukeshwar Dutt was sentenced to transportation for life, while Bhagat Singh was tried in the Lahore Conspiracy Case.

 

NOTE

 

• 1 and 2 only (Option 1): Including statement 2 is a mistake, because the intention was not to cause deaths; the explosives were deliberately low-intensity and thrown into an open space.

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 3): Pairing statements 2 and 3 accepts the false claim about killing members and rejects the true claim about the two throwers, so it is incorrect.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): All three cannot be right since the aim of the act was protest and publicity of their ideas, not murder of legislators.

question:
Match the revolutionary event with its place.

Column A: (a) Kakori train action (b) Throwing of bombs in Central Legislative Assembly (c) Death of Chandra Shekhar Azad (d) Killing of J.P. Saunders

Column B: (i) Delhi (ii) Lahore (iii) Alfred Park, Allahabad (iv) Near Lucknow
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iv, b-i, c-iii, d-ii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kakori train action of 1925 took place at a village near Lucknow (a-iv) (क्रांतिकारी घटनाएँ और उनके स्थान)

 

• The bombs of 8 April 1929 were thrown in the Central Legislative Assembly at Delhi (b-i)

 

• Chandra Shekhar Azad shot himself in Alfred Park, Allahabad on 27 February 1931 when surrounded by police (c-iii)

 

• J.P. Saunders was killed at Lahore in 1928 (d-ii).

 

• Hence the interpretation depends on place: Alfred Park in Allahabad, a village near Lucknow, the capital's Assembly hall and a city of Punjab are four different sites.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Alfred Park at Allahabad has since been renamed Chandra Shekhar Azad Park.

 

• Azad's slogan was that he would remain 'Azad' (free) all his life.

 

• The Lahore Conspiracy Case covered the Saunders murder.

 

• The Lahore Conspiracy Case was tried by a special tribunal created by an ordinance after the accused boycotted the proceedings.

 

NOTE

 

• a-i, b-iv, c-iii, d-ii (Option 1): This arrangement swaps Delhi and Lucknow's neighbourhood so that Kakori is wrongly placed in Delhi and the Assembly bombing near Lucknow, which reverses two correct pairs.

 

• a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i (Option 2): Matching the Assembly bombing to Lahore and the Saunders killing to Delhi interchanges the sites; the bombing was in the capital while Saunders fell at Lahore.

 

• a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii (Option 3): Here Azad's death is pushed to Lucknow and Kakori placed at Alfred Park, but Allahabad is where Azad died and Kakori is a village by Lucknow.
